::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [February 1854]  
**From:** [Otterbourne]  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown.  This fragment printed in Romanes, <i>[Appreciation](other_books/otherbook_241.qmd)</i> p. 76
:::

Dear, good [old slave](people/person_113.qmd),
How nice and kind and understanding your letter was, and how thankful one should be for such friends! ...

The worst will be over when we hear from [Julian](people/person_1624.qmd), poor boy! Till then it seems like bearing the first stroke. But I am sure it fell mercifully as far as we were concerned, and the flow of feelings that meet us from all is very gratifying.

I believe [my uncle](people/person_1614.qmd), always living in his own town far off, had no notion of the estimation in which his brother was held.

. . . I know I shall miss [him](people/person_1631.qmd) more when he has been away longer.
